fulltext: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，据彭博社报道，Anthropic 公司敦促华盛顿联邦上诉法院重新审议此前的一项判决，该判决维持了特朗普政府将这家人工智能企业认定为危害美国国家安全供应链风险主体的决定。
该公司于当地时间周二申请由上诉法院全体法官，复核一个三人法官小组在 9 月 25 日以 2 比 1 票数作出的裁决。Anthropic 主张，多数意见对法律作出了错误解读，允许美国国防部“在没有任何预先认定流程的情况下采取行动，而且已有明确证据表明，这项认定是对 Anthropic 就人工智能安全公开发表言论的报复”。
Anthropic 与政府之间的这场法律博弈事关重大。在人工智能技术发展的关键节点，法院需要判定，究竟是联邦政府还是私营企业掌握人工智能技术安全防护机制的控制权。美国本土开发者正争相推出最先进的人工智能模型，并向投资者证明这项技术能够实现盈利。
今年早些时候，双方关于军方使用该公司人工智能技术的合同谈判破裂，Anthropic 由此与特朗普政府公开产生争执。
这家公司曾要求获得保证，其技术不会被用于对美国民众的大规模监控，或是自主武器部署。但美方表示，出于国家安全考量，无法接受对技术使用施加任何限制。
美国国防部在 3 月通知 Anthropic，该企业及其产品被认定为美国供应链风险，所有联邦机构都需要撤回和这家公司相关的业务指令。这类风险认定，以往一般只针对美国视作对手国家的企业。
Anthropic 对政府提起两起诉讼，一起在加州，针对国防部要求联邦机构停止和该公司合作的指令；另一起向哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院提起，质疑这项风险认定本身的合法性。
在旧金山的案件中 Anthropic 胜诉，美国地区法官丽塔 ·F· 林（Rita F. Lin）在 8 月下令，要求政府解除联邦机构使用 Anthropic 技术的禁令。她强调，国防部此举的动机看起来属于报复，而非出于正当的安全考量。
但在华盛顿的这起案件里，三人法官小组于 9 月 25 日裁定，政府的这项认定具备合法性。
格雷戈里 · 卡察斯（Gregory Katsas）法官撰写多数意见称，国防部“有合理理由担心，Anthropic 可能修改克劳德（Claude）模型的设计，使其无法执行国防部认为在合同授权范围内、且具备必要性的国家安全相关任务”。
IT之家注意到，本案案号为 Anthropic 诉美国国防部案，26-01049，受理法院为美国哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院（华盛顿）。

Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman believes we’re nearing a future where everyone will have an AI appliance in their own home.

Speaking on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on Tuesday, the chipmaker executive answered a question about what would need to happen for AI to become a home appliance, saying, “Actually, I don’t think that’s very far away.”
He pointed to the advances in consumer AI agents, like Meta’s Muse and Instinct, the startup now valued at $10 billion, as examples of how AI is finding its footing with everyday users.
As for home AI? He predicts that we’ll have personal AI assistants that run locally.

“Just like your cell phone, they’ll do some work on device and some work going back to the cloud,” Feldman explained. “But I think they will get to know you very well, and you will have a security perimeter around them. And they will certainly have access to credit cards and be able to buy things for you,” he continued. “I think they will make a meaningful impact in making our lives better.”
Of course, for an AI chipmaker, the vision of a home AI appliance, or at least widespread consumer adoption of agentic technology, is certainly appealing.

But Feldman isn’t just working on the hardware infrastructure; he’s a personal AI user himself, saying that he now uses “a collection of agents” to sweep his calendar, pull up information about the people he’s going to have a call with, and more. While AI is already doing many of the things we used to do manually, Feldman is most excited about the new possibilities — things that weren’t possible before.
He’s leaving it up to other founders to figure out what those might be, though.
“One of the reasons I love being in infrastructure is because I don’t need the consumer-facing idea … I like building the platforms that other people’s ideas take flight on,” he said.

Cerebras Systems 首席执行官兼联合创始人安德鲁·费尔德曼 (Andrew Feldman) 相信，我们即将迎来这样一个未来：每个人都将在自己的家中拥有人工智能设备。
周二，这位芯片制造商高管在 TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 的舞台上发表讲话，回答了有关人工智能成为家用电器需要做什么的问题，他说：“实际上，我认为这离实现并不遥远。”
他指出消费者人工智能代理的进步，例如 Meta 的 Muse 和 Instinct（这家初创公司目前估值 100 亿美元），作为人工智能如何在日常用户中站稳脚跟的例子。
至于家庭人工智能？他预测我们将拥有在本地运行的个人人工智能助理。
“就像你的手机一样，它们会在设备上完成一些工作，并在云端完成一些工作，”费尔德曼解释道。 “但我认为他们会非常了解你，你周围会有一个安全边界。他们肯定可以使用信用卡并能够为你买东西，”他继续说道。 “我认为它们将对改善我们的生活产生有意义的影响。”
当然，对于人工智能芯片制造商来说，家用人工智能设备的愿景，或者至少是消费者广泛采用代理技术，无疑是有吸引力的。
但费尔德曼不仅仅致力于硬件基础设施；他还致力于开发硬件基础设施。他本人就是一名个人人工智能用户，他说他现在使用“一组代理”来扫描他的日历，提取有关他将要通话的人的信息等等。虽然人工智能已经可以完成我们过去手动完成的许多事情，但费尔德曼对新的可能性感到最兴奋——以前不可能的事情。
不过，他将留给其他创始人来弄清楚这些可能是什么。
“我喜欢从事基础设施行业的原因之一是因为我不需要面向消费者的想法……我喜欢构建其他人的想法得以飞翔的平台，”他说。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，据路透社报道，美国特拉华州一个陪审团于当地时间周二认定，芯片技术供应商 Arm Holdings 违反了与高通（Qualcomm）的许可协议，还故意干扰这家芯片厂商与 Meta 公司的业务往来，但仅裁定 2 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 13.4 元人民币）的象征性赔偿金。
这项判决出自上周为期五天的庭审，这也是两家企业两年内的第二次诉讼，案件凸显双方业务关系持续恶化。软银集团在 2016 年取得 Arm 控制权之后，Arm 的业务重心从授权芯片制造所需技术，转向自研芯片销售，双方矛盾随之加剧。
判决出炉后，Arm 股价下跌 1%，高通股价上涨 1%，不过高通股价相比判决前约 2.4% 的涨幅已有小幅回落。
两家企业都对判决中的部分内容表示认可，而案件部分核心争议仍悬而未决。
高通在一份声明中表示：“陪审团认定 Arm 违反了和高通长期生效的架构许可协议（ALA），没有履行承诺，并且刻意采取行动扰乱高通业务，我们对此感到欣慰。”
Arm 方面称：“高通提起本次诉讼，试图依据许可协议剥夺 Arm 数十亿美元收益。但陪审团的判决证实，Arm 在技术许可协议的履约过程中秉持善意，仅判定 2 美元（现汇率约合 13.4 元人民币）赔偿金，也证明 Arm 在本案中的主张具备合理性。”
陪审团认定，Arm 没有履行义务，未能为自家芯片设计提供软件补丁与配套工具。而其余五项违约指控，陪审团判定 Arm 胜诉。
陪审团同时认定，Arm 存在故意以及过失干扰高通与 Meta 合作关系的行为。高通称，2024 年其本即将和 Meta 达成合作，而 Arm 被指向彭博新闻社泄露高通违反许可协议的消息，致使这份和 Meta 的合作协议被推迟。
针对这两项指控，陪审团各裁定 1 美元（现汇率约合 6.7 元人民币）象征性赔偿。相关认定也为高通保留了后续主张权利的空间，案件将进入下一阶段，由美国地区法官玛丽埃伦 · 诺雷卡（Maryellen Noreika）处理多项争议。
法院认定违约这一结果，意味着诺雷卡有可能据此裁定，高通可在五年内停止向 Arm 支付专利费，这笔费用价值或达数十亿美元。Arm 主张，许可协议条款中这项为期五年的专利费处罚不具备强制执行力。
陪审团关于业务干扰的认定，可被高通用来佐证其观点，即 Arm 没有就下一代技术开展善意谈判，该争议同样需要法官作出裁决。
针对这部分裁决结果，败诉一方大概率会提起上诉。

Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman thinks the AI doomer narrative isn’t doing the industry any favors. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, the AI chipmaker exec quipped that “some of the leaders in the AI world maybe shouldn’t be allowed to talk in public.”

He’s referencing the negativity now spreading around the dangers of AI, from models breaking containment to AI insiders debating the percentage chance that AI may kill all of humanity by the end of the decade. The argument has become so mainstream that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei was recently parodied in a skit on “Saturday Night Live,” where the fictional character summed up the discourse, saying, “We do not condone what we are doing.”

Feldman, however, thinks the promise and potential that go hand in hand with AI developments are getting overlooked. He thinks AI leaders should spend more time telling people that AI could lead to a world where your grandkids will “never meet anybody who dies of cancer,” for instance, even if they have concerns about AI risks.

Clearly, Feldman has a vested interest in AI being successful, as the company’s customers include big names working with the technology, like OpenAI, Block, Figma, pharmaceutical giant GSK, and Lovable.
However, he’s pragmatic about weighing the trade-offs between risk and reward.

“I don’t think there are powerful technologies that don’t come with the challenge of ‘what happens when powerful technologies are in the hands of bad people?’ I think you can’t make one and not have the other,” Feldman said during his interview at Disrupt.
“I think what we have to say is that this technology is powerful,” he added. “We have to be thoughtful about it. We have to regulate it reasonably,” he added.
The chipmaker CEO also suggested that some of the negativity around AI has to do with how the data center industry has approached the new buildouts created by AI demand.

“As an industry, we weren’t super good for the past few years at working with local communities, particularly in the U.S. We — the industry — didn’t do what others have done in the power industry in oil and gas. They didn’t work with the community. They didn’t engage the community as they should have, and that was a problem,” Feldman said.

He compared the NIMBY-ism — “not in my backyard!” — of what’s going on in the U.S. with other countries, naming Brazil, Canada, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Mexico, and Sweden as markets where they’re encouraging companies to build data centers.
Feldman also wasn’t concerned that efficiency improvements would create less demand for his chips, or those from other companies competing with Nvidia, as Cerebras is.

“We can do our job as hardware vendors to make our compute more efficient, and then the model makers can do improved work in making their models more efficient to achieve the same goals. All of this has to come together to make meaningful strides forward,” he noted.

“我认为我们不得不说的是这项技术非常强大，”他补充道。 “我们必须深思熟虑。我们必须合理监管，”他补充道。
这位芯片制造商首席执行官还表示，围绕人工智能的一些负面因素与数据中心行业如何应对人工智能需求带来的新扩建有关。
“作为一个行业，过去几年我们在与当地社区合作方面表现得不太好，尤其是在美国。我们这个行业没有做其他人在石油和天然气电力行业所做的事情。他们没有与社区合作。他们没有像应有的那样让社区参与进来，这是一个问题，”费尔德曼说。
他比较了邻避主义——“不要在我的后院！” - 美国与其他国家正在发生的事情，指出巴西、加拿大、芬兰、冰岛、挪威、墨西哥和瑞典是他们鼓励公司建立数据中心的市场。
费尔德曼也不担心效率的提高会减少对他的芯片或与 Nvidia 竞争的其他公司（如 Cerebras）的芯片的需求。
“作为硬件供应商，我们可以做好我们的工作，使我们的计算更加高效，然后模型制作者可以改进工作，使他们的模型更加高效，以实现相同的目标。所有这些必须结合在一起才能取得有意义的进步，”他指出。

cards.title: It’s ‘incomprehensible’ that Instagram allowed an AI image of Mia Goth to spread, say her reps
cards.title_cn: Instagram 允许 Mia Goth 的人工智能图像传播，她的代表表示，这是“不可理解的”
cards.summary: 【The Verge】Earlier this month, news broke that actress Mia Goth had filed for divorce from actor and filmmaker Shia LaBeouf. An Instagram post from the account miagoth_ - marked with a blue verified checkmark -…
fulltext: A viral photo purporting to show Mia Goth in a T-shirt seemingly referencing her divorce spread from Instagram across the web. It was AI.﻿

Earlier this month, news broke that actress Mia Goth had filed for divorce from actor and filmmaker Shia LaBeouf. An Instagram post from the account miagoth_ — marked with a blue verified checkmark — quickly spread.

The post shows Goth in a T-shirt that reads “MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN” in bold black letters. The Beyoncé song “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)” had been added to the Instagram post. Hundreds of thousands of people — including some in the entertainment industry — liked the image, and entertainment outlets like OK! and even People wrote about it as if it were authentic. Soon, screenshots of the post were shared widely on other social media platforms.
But the image, Goth’s representatives say, was AI-generated, posted by an account they had asked Instagram to remove.

“Mia Goth does not have ownership of, nor does she engage in social media on any platform. We have filed multiple complaints with Instagram to remove the verified fan account which continues to post counterfeit, AI images of Mia Goth,” Christine Tripicchio, a representative for Goth, told The Verge in an email. “The fact that this fan account meets Instagram’s criteria to qualify for a ‘blue check’ is disconcerting on a fundamental level. Beyond that, it is incomprehensible that Instagram evidently prioritizes the dissemination of forged and manipulated images over the protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.”

The miagoth_ account was labeled as fan-run, but the blue checkmark — which for years signaled an official, authentic entity — likely caused confusion for many in and out of the industry (the page had over a million followers). Meta began selling blue checkmarks several years ago as part of a new program, allowing accounts like the fan page to secure “verified” badges even if they weren’t run by the person being depicted in content.
Meta spokesperson Alex Dziedzan told The Verge the miagoth_ account was removed for impersonating a public figure.

Rather than ban AI-generated content of real people, Meta has taken the approach of labeling some content created with generative AI. Photorealistic AI videos of people, for example, may require an AI label — but Meta’s own rules include a carve-out that the label is not required for still images. AI-generated content featuring real people, including public figures, regularly racks up millions of views on Instagram, and Meta executives have signaled that AI-generated content will be a key part of how users engage on the company’s platforms going forward.

Entertainers including musicians and actors have for years raised concerns about their likenesses being used to generate AI content. In 2024, Scarlett Johansson said that OpenAI had used a soundalike for the voice of ChatGPT even after she declined to work with the company on the project. That same year, Taylor Swift endorsed Kamala Harris for president, saying AI-generated images of her posted by Donald Trump made her realize she needed to “combat misinformation” around who she would be voting for.

fulltext_cn: 一张病毒照片在 Instagram 上疯传，照片中米娅·高斯 (Mia Goth) 身穿 T 恤，似乎在提及她的离婚经历。这是人工智能。﻿
本月早些时候，有消息称女演员米娅·高斯已向演员兼电影制片人希亚·拉博夫提出离婚。来自 miagoth_ 帐户的 Instagram 帖子（标有蓝色验证复选标记）迅速传播开来。
帖子中，Goth 穿着一件 T 恤，上面用粗体黑色字母写着“MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN”（我的前男友是我最大的粉丝）。碧昂丝的歌曲“单身女士（戴上戒指）”已添加到 Instagram 帖子中。数十万人——包括娱乐界的一些人——喜欢这张照片，娱乐媒体也喜欢《OK！》甚至连《人物》杂志都把它写得好像它是真实的一样。很快，该帖子的截图在其他社交媒体平台上广泛传播。
但 Goth 的代表表示，这张图片是人工智能生成的，是由他们要求 Instagram 删除的一个账户发布的。

Goth 的代表 Christine Tripicchio 在一封电子邮件中告诉 The Verge：“Mia Goth 没有任何社交媒体的所有权，也没有在任何平台上参与社交媒体活动。我们已向 Instagram 提出多项投诉，要求删除经过验证的粉丝帐户，该帐户继续发布 Mia Goth 的假冒 AI 图像。” “这个粉丝账户符合 Instagram 获得‘蓝色支票’的标准，这一事实从根本上来说令人不安。除此之外，令人难以理解的是，Instagram 显然优先考虑传播伪造和操纵的图像，而不是公众人物肖像的保护和完整性。”
miagoth_ 帐户被标记为粉丝运行，但蓝色复选标记（多年来一直标志着一个官方的、真实的实体）可能会给行业内外的许多人带来困惑（该页面拥有超过 100 万粉丝）。 Meta 几年前开始销售蓝色复选标记，作为新计划的一部分，允许粉丝页面等帐户获得“经过验证”的徽章，即使它们不是由内容中描述的人运行的。
Meta 发言人 Alex Dziedzan 告诉 The Verge，miagoth_ 帐户因冒充公众人物而被删除。
Meta 并没有禁止人工智能生成真人内容，而是采取了标记一些用生成人工智能创建的内容的方法。例如，逼真的人工智能人物视频可能需要人工智能标签，但 Meta 自己的规则包括一个例外，即静态图像不需要标签。以包括公众人物在内的真人为主角的人工智能生成内容经常在 Instagram 上获得数百万次浏览量，Meta 高管表示，人工智能生成的内容将成为用户未来如何参与该公司平台的关键部分。

多年来，包括音乐家和演员在内的艺人一直对他们的肖像被用来生成人工智能内容表示担忧。 2024 年，斯嘉丽·约翰逊 (Scarlett Johansson) 表示，即使在她拒绝与该公司合作开展该项目后，OpenAI 仍使用了与 ChatGPT 声音相似的声音。同年，泰勒·斯威夫特支持卡玛拉·哈里斯竞选总统，称唐纳德·特朗普发布的人工智能生成的她的图像让她意识到她需要“打击关于她将投票给谁的错误信息”。

A judge has ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI’s hiring materials in the trade secrets-focused lawsuit the iPhone maker filed against OpenAI in July.

Specifically, the court will allow Apple to view documents associated with OpenAI’s interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles within its consumer hardware and robotics groups ahead of the rumored launch of OpenAI’s first hardware device.

These documents could include interview checklists, guides, instructions, manuals, and scripts, as well as technical presentations and records showing that interview discussions had included references to Apple technology or components.

The court gave OpenAI five days to turn over materials it has already collected and 14 days for any other materials related to this request, agreeing with Apple that these documents should be expedited.

The case comes as OpenAI develops a consumer hardware device that could one day potentially rival the iPhone — or smartphones more generally — if the AI device becomes a central part of consumers’ lives and how they engage with software and services.

In its lawsuit, Apple accused OpenAI of a pattern of theft, which includes direct complaints about former employees using Apple laptops to download confidential material and files that contained information about unannounced technologies, features, and products, including technical specifications, engineering presentations, and proprietary project data.
Apple also said that former Apple employees at OpenAI coached others considering leaving Apple for OpenAI on what information to bring to their interviews, among other allegations.

U.S. District Judge Edward Davila didn’t greenlight all of Apple’s requests for expedited access to OpenAI documents and messages relevant to the case. But he did rule that Apple could access the interview materials, alongside private LINE messages (from a messaging app) between individuals named in the case, including OpenAI employees Chang Liu and Alyssa Peng.
The judge also approved depositions for Liu and Peng, along with a third individual, OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, Tang Yew Tan. All three are former Apple employees.

However, the judge denied Apple’s request to expedite its access to OpenAI’s research and development in specific areas, like metal finishes and power management. He also denied several of Apple’s broader discovery requests, like access to OpenAI’s hardware research or information about what its former employees created while working at OpenAI.
That denial isn’t final, though; the judge left the door open for Apple to narrow its requests and try again.

法官裁定，苹果公司将在 7 月份针对 OpenAI 提起的以商业机密为重点的诉讼中快速获取 OpenAI 的招聘材料。
具体来说，法院将允许苹果查看与 OpenAI 采访前苹果员工相关的文件，这些前苹果员工在传闻中的 OpenAI 首款硬件设备推出之前申请了消费硬件和机器人团队的职位。
这些文件可能包括面试清单、指南、说明、手册和脚本，以及显示面试讨论中引用了苹果技术或组件的技术演示和记录。
法院给了 OpenAI 5 天的时间来移交其已经收集的材料，并给了 14 天的时间来移交与此请求相关的任何其他材料，并同意苹果公司应加快处理这些文件。
此案发生之际，OpenAI 正在开发一种消费类硬件设备，如果该 AI 设备成为消费者生活以及他们如何使用软件和服务的核心部分，那么该设备有一天可能会与 iPhone（或更广泛的智能手机）相媲美。
苹果在诉讼中指控 OpenAI 存在盗窃行为，其中包括直接投诉前员工使用苹果笔记本电脑下载机密材料和文件，其中包含有关未宣布的技术、功能和产品的信息，包括技术规格、工程演示和专有项目数据。
苹果还表示，OpenAI 的前苹果员工对其他考虑离开苹果前往 OpenAI 的人进行了指导，告诉他们面试时应携带哪些信息等。
美国地区法官爱德华·达维拉 (Edward Davila) 并未批准苹果公司提出的所有加快获取与本案相关的 OpenAI 文件和消息的请求。但他确实裁定，苹果公司可以访问采访材料，以及案件中点名的个人（包括 OpenAI 员工 Chang Liu 和 Alyssa Peng）之间的私人 LINE 消息（来自消息应用程序）。
法官还批准了刘和彭以及第三个人、OpenAI 首席硬件官 Tang Yew Tan 的证词。这三人都是前苹果员工。
然而，法官拒绝了苹果公司要求加快其参与 OpenAI 在金属表面处理和电源管理等特定领域的研发的请求。他还拒绝了苹果公司的一些更广泛的发现请求，例如访问 OpenAI 的硬件研究或有关其前员工在 OpenAI 工作期间创建的内容的信息。
不过，这种否认还不是最终的。法官为苹果公司缩小要求范围并再次尝试留下了余地。

cards.title: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
cards.title_cn: Xbox 正式拥抱 AI 驱动的游戏端口的混乱
cards.summary: 【The Verge】Retro gaming is going through a wild time at the moment, thanks to decompilations and recompilations that are letting gamers port classic titles to new devices, or merge code from two different games…
fulltext: Microsoft has created a new Xbox Labs group to experiment with decompiling and recompiling games.

Retro gaming is going through a wild time at the moment, thanks to decompilations and recompilations that are letting gamers port classic titles to new devices, or merge code from two different games into a single new experience. Microsoft has witnessed skateboarding being modded into Call of Duty and Halo being played in a web browser, and the company is now officially embracing the chaos of this new AI-powered era of game modding.

Microsoft is putting together a new Xbox Labs group to explore the rapid emergence of these mods, many of which use AI models to help modders remix games in ways we’ve rarely seen before. Xbox Labs will be a “small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience,” says Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. “We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.”

Sharma thinks the experiments we’ve seen in recent weeks, where Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside browsers, “challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games.”

“While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators,” says Sharma. “These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.“

Modders are now doing the type of work that Microsoft has been doing for decades with its Xbox backward compatibility program, letting old games run on modern hardware. But they’re doing it without the business model restrictions that Microsoft is tied to. It’s starting to feel like we’re just a model or two away from even more breakthroughs that decouple more modern games from their intended hardware.

Sharma clearly sees an opportunity here, particularly for AI agent use at Xbox. “I think Xbox has an important role to play here,” says Sharma. “Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide.”

Xbox Labs is clearly a way for Microsoft to experiment with how AI will shape where games are played, and Xbox will share any tools and learnings with developers. The bigger question is how Microsoft will respond to decompiles and recompiles of games where modders take its precious IP and make it freely available. Modding is fun, but I can’t see Microsoft and other publishers seeing the fun side if modern console games start to appear where they shouldn’t.
I asked Microsoft to comment about unauthorized IP use, but the company didn’t respond in time for publication.
Here’s Sharma’s full memo:

The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we’ve helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.

In recent weeks, we’ve seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.

These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models. To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.

I think XBOX has an important role to play here. Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We’ve spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.

Our priorities aren’t changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway.

复古游戏目前正在经历一段疯狂的时期，这要归功于反编译和重新编译，让游戏玩家可以将经典游戏移植到新设备上，或者将两个不同游戏的代码合并到一个新的体验中。微软见证了滑板被改装成在网络浏览器中玩的《使命召唤》和《光环》，该公司现在正式接受这个由人工智能驱动的游戏改装新时代的混乱。

微软正在组建一个新的 Xbox 实验室小组来探索这些模组的快速出现，其中许多模组使用人工智能模型来帮助改装者以我们以前很少见过的方式重新混合游戏。 Xbox 首席执行官阿莎·夏尔马 (Asha Sharma) 表示，Xbox 实验室将是一个“由游戏制作者、工程师和科学家组成的小团体，他们的工作是将新兴想法转化为我们的玩家和开发者可以体验的东西”。 “我们将开放地构建，向人们的行为学习，并通过是否有更多的人在玩和创造来衡量成功。”
Sharma 认为，我们最近几周看到的实验（其中 Windows PC 版本已被转换为在 Apple Silicon 上运行或移植为在浏览器内部运行）“挑战了我们行业长期以来的假设：软件和硬件之间的联系、创作和游戏之间的界限，以及人们如何发现和体验游戏。”
“虽然很难预测游戏的未来，但很容易看到让优秀游戏更容易访问、赋予旧游戏新生命以及让更多玩家成为创造者和共同创造者的可能性，”夏尔马说。 “对于玩家来说，这些无疑是良好的结果，即使（有时是因为）他们挑战了我们现有的商业模式。”
改装者现在正在做微软几十年来一直在做的工作，即 Xbox 向后兼容计划，让旧游戏可以在现代硬件上运行。但他们这样做并没有受到微软所依赖的商业模式限制。人们开始感觉我们距离更多突破只有一两个模型之遥，这些突破将更多现代游戏与其预期的硬件脱钩。
Sharma 清楚地看到了这里的机会，特别是在 Xbox 上使用人工智能代理。 “我认为 Xbox 在这里可以发挥重要作用，”Sharma 说。 “编码成为代理的首要工作量，因为他们可以编写、运行和测试软件。游戏具有许多相同的属性，人们每年花在 XBOX 游戏上的时间超过 720 亿小时，大约是全球估计编写代码时间的五倍。”
Xbox 实验室显然是微软尝试人工智能如何塑造游戏玩法的一种方式，Xbox 将与开发者分享任何工具和学习成果。更大的问题是，微软将如何应对修改者获取其宝贵知识产权并免费提供的游戏的反编译和重新编译。改装很有趣，但如果现代主机游戏开始出现在不该出现的地方，我看不到微软和其他发行商看到乐趣的一面。
我要求微软对未经授权的知识产权使用发表评论，但该公司没有及时做出回应。
这是夏尔马的完整备忘录：
第一批电子游戏出现于大约 75 年前。从那时起，有过繁荣和萧条，但每年都有更多精彩的游戏可供玩，有更多的设备可供玩，最重要的是，玩游戏的人比以往任何时候都多。这种增长帮助 XBOX 取得了今天的成就，作为回报，我们也帮助塑造了这个行业，从通过 Xbox Live 将硬盘引入游戏机和在线游戏，到 Game Pass 和云游戏，以及将数百万人聚集在一起的特许经营权。
最近几周，我们看到游戏被快速反编译和重建，以便在它们最初设计时从未支持的硬件上运行。 Windows PC 版本已被转换为在 Apple Silicon 上运行，或通过 WebAssembly 和 WebGPU 移植到浏览器内运行，后者目前已接近 90% 的全球浏览器支持。也许更令人惊讶的是，我们看到世界上许多最大的游戏都被重新混合到另一个游戏的源代码中。

这些实验挑战了我们行业长期以来的假设：软件和硬件之间的联系、创作和游戏之间的界限，以及人们如何发现和体验游戏。虽然很难预测游戏的未来，但很容易看到让优秀游戏更容易访问、赋予老游戏新生命以及让更多玩家成为创造者和共同创造者的可能性。对于玩家来说，这些无疑是良好的结果，即使（有时是因为）他们挑战了我们现有的商业模式。为了探索这些可能性，我请 Scott 组建了 XBOX LABS，这是一个由游戏制作者、工程师和科学家组成的小组，他们的工作是将新兴想法转化为我们的玩家和开发者可以体验的东西。我们将开放地构建，向人们学习，并通过是否有更多的人在玩和创造来衡量成功。
我认为 XBOX 在这里可以发挥重要作用。编码成为代理的首要工作负载，因为他们可以编写、运行和测试软件。游戏具有许多相同的属性，人们每年花在 XBOX 游戏上的时间超过 720 亿小时，大约是全球估计编写代码时间的五倍。我们花了 25 年的时间学习如何制作出色的游戏，我希望我们的游戏制作者能够帮助塑造这些新技术的成果。随着我们的学习，我们将一如既往地与整个行业的开发人员分享我们构建的工具。
我们的优先事项没有改变。我们仍然致力于 4C、制作出色的游戏、我们的硬件以及成为知识产权及其周围社区的负责任的管理者。 LABS 为我们提供了一种探索新技术的方法，同时又不放弃已经正在进行的工作。

When I was eight, I remember our train to Mumbai ground to a halt with a great noise. When we started moving again, a good eight hours later, someone pointed out a mangled tail, of all things, hanging from a branch close to the tracks.

The train, you see, had apparently hit a wild bison at full speed, and the impact damaged the engine so badly that it had to be towed away for repairs. For a long time, I thought such things only happened in places like rural India, but I learned a few years ago that wildlife and infrastructure do not mix anywhere on the planet.

The FAA estimates that wildlife strikes have cost U.S. civil aviation about $272 million a year on average between 1990 and 2025. In France, the rail operator SNCF says wandering animals affect more than 8,000 trains across the country each year and are among its five leading causes of delays. In Brittany, 120 trains hit animals in 2023 alone, disrupting 660 services and causing more than 15,000 minutes of delays.

Reading about all that damage, to both infrastructure and animals, inspired Sara Nozkova (pictured above on the left) to develop a wildlife-deterrent system that works differently from the sirens, lights, fences, falcons, and culling traditionally used to keep animals away from roads, train tracks, airports, and other infrastructure.
“I was convinced the answer was not a louder deterrent,” she told TechCrunch.

After spending 13 years working in transportation and autonomous vehicles, Nozkova had learned how quickly the systems we build to navigate roads and other controlled environments fail once nature enters the equation.

“We have taught machines to be brilliant, but only inside the environments we engineered for them,” she said. “Cities, factory lines, warehouses. Fixed geometry, known objects. Stepping outside into nature, I saw firsthand how the same machines quickly go blind. Because nature is complex and always alive.”

So instead she joined the AI lab at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm and started working on a system that could change its deterrent responses based on what an animal nearby is doing, and even what kind of animal it is.

That work turned into Flox Intelligence, which spun out of KTH in 2020 and is one of the finalists at this year’s Startup Battlefield 200 pitch competition at TechCrunch Disrupt, taking place this year at Moscone West in San Francisco October 13-15.

Flox makes edge devices that process data on-site rather than in the cloud. Like autonomous vehicles, they use perception systems to sense their surroundings, but theirs are trained on wildlife behavior. A motion sensor wakes the device when it detects movement, triggering a camera that uses on-device models to identify nearby animals. The device then emits a species-appropriate sound to scare them away.
Nozkova says the system learns from experience, too, and varies its responses so animals don’t get habituated to repeated signals.

The company currently sells battery-operated devices that can be mounted on poles, trees, and other structures. It also offers a software platform that shows clients where the devices are deployed and what’s happening on the ground. The platform can also generate reports for regulatory compliance and for uses like biodiversity monitoring. The longer-term goal is to make the software portable enough to run on machines that work outside, including trains, cars, and drones.

Nozkova says about 150 Flox devices are live in North America, Europe, and Australia at airfields and airport perimeters, road and rail corridors (especially fence ends and crossings along wildlife corridors), national parks, agricultural land, urban areas, mining sites, and critical infrastructure such as electrical substations.

The company sells edge units up front, then charges an annual software and AI subscription after the first year. Flox also has OEM partnerships with companies that pay an annual fee to deploy its software on vehicles, like trains. Train manufacturer Alstom is one such partner.
The company expects to end 2026 with revenue of about $1.5 million, Nozkova said.

As unique as Flox’s product and approach are, the startup is not without competition. Robin Radar’s Scarecrow also uses species-specific distress calls to disperse birds and it records the activity, while iCHASE sells a system that detects birds with computer vision and targets them with a moving laser, adjusting its response as needed.
Nozkova says her moat is the breadth of the system and the data Flox has collected in the field, which she calls “ground truth on what actually makes a moose or a grizzly bear move safely.”

“Physical AI is walking out of the factory and into the messy, alive outdoors,” Nozkova says. “Every machine that operates outside — trains, trucks, drones, tractors, robots — will need to understand nature, and nature intelligence is the next layer of the perception stack. Almost nobody is building it.”

The company has raised about $5 million across pre-seed and seed rounds so far, with the seed round led by Unconventional Ventures and Tilia Impact Ventures. Co-investors across the rounds include GENIUS NY, Norrsken, Satgana, and angel investors, Nozkova said.

The company is now opening a $10 million Series A, which would mostly go toward growing from about 150 devices to several thousand deployed units and extending the underlying system beyond its current wildlife use cases.

我八岁的时候，我记得开往孟买的火车在一声巨响中停了下来。八个小时后，当我们再次开始移动时，有人指出了一条残破的尾巴，挂在靠近铁轨的树枝上。
你看，这列火车显然全速撞上了一头野牛，撞击严重损坏了发动机，不得不将其拖走进行修理。很长一段时间，我认为这样的事情只会发生在像印度农村这样的地方，但几年前我了解到，野生动物和基础设施在地球上的任何地方都不会混合。
美国联邦航空局估计，1990 年至 2025 年间，野生动物袭击平均每年给美国民航造成约 2.72 亿美元的损失。在法国，铁路运营商 SNCF 表示，流浪动物每年影响全国 8,000 多列火车，是造成延误的五个主要原因之一。在布列塔尼，仅 2023 年就有 120 趟火车撞上动物，导致 660 趟列车中断，并造成超过 15,000 分钟的延误。
了解到这些对基础设施和动物造成的损害后，萨拉·诺兹科娃（Sara Nozkova）（上图左上图）受到启发，开发了一种野生动物威慑系统，该系统的工作原理不同于传统上用于让动物远离道路、铁轨、机场和其他基础设施的警报器、灯光、栅栏、猎鹰和扑杀。
“我确信这个答案不会产生更大的威慑力，”她告诉 TechCrunch。
在交通和自动驾驶汽车领域工作了 13 年之后，诺兹科娃了解到，一旦自然因素介入，我们为道路和其他受控环境导航而构建的系统会很快失效。
“我们教机器变得聪明，但仅限于我们为它们设计的环境中，”她说。 “城市、工厂生产线、仓库。固定的几何形状、已知的物体。走进大自然，我亲眼目睹了同样的机器如何很快失明。因为大自然是复杂的，而且总是充满活力的。”
因此，她加入了斯德哥尔摩 KTH 皇家理工学院的人工智能实验室，并开始开发一个系统，该系统可以根据附近动物的行为，甚至是动物的种类来改变其威慑反应。
这项工作后来发展成为 Flox Intelligence，该公司于 2020 年从 KTH 分拆出来，是今年 TechCrunch Disrupt 初创公司战场 200 场竞赛的决赛入围者之一，该竞赛将于今年 10 月 13 日至 15 日在旧金山 Moscone West 举行。
Flox 制造的边缘设备可以在现场而不是在云端处理数据。与自动驾驶汽车一样，它们使用感知系统来感知周围环境，但它们的系统接受了野生动物行为的训练。运动传感器在检测到运动时会唤醒设备，触发相机使用设备上的模型来识别附近的动物。然后，该设备会发出适合物种的声音来吓跑它们。
诺兹科娃说，该系统也会从经验中学习，并改变其反应，这样动物就不会习惯重复的信号。
该公司目前销售可安装在电线杆、树木和其他结构上的电池供电设备。它还提供了一个软件平台，向客户展示设备的部署位置以及现场发生的情况。该平台还可以生成报告以供监管合规性和生物多样性监测等用途。长期目标是使软件具有足够的便携性，可以在户外工作的机器上运行，包括火车、汽车和无人机。
Nozkova 表示，北美、欧洲和澳大利亚的机场和机场周边、公路和铁路走廊（特别是野生动物走廊沿线的栅栏末端和交叉口）、国家公园、农业用地、城市地区、矿区以及变电站等关键基础设施内部署了大约 150 台 Flox 设备。
该公司预先销售边缘设备，然后在第一年后收取年度软件和人工智能订阅费用。 Flox 还与一些公司建立了 OEM 合作伙伴关系，这些公司支付年费将其软件部署在火车等车辆上。火车制造商阿尔斯通就是这样的合作伙伴之一。
Nozkova 表示，该公司预计到 2026 年底营收将达到约 150 万美元。
尽管 Flox 的产品和方法非常独特，但这家初创公司并非没有竞争。 Robin Radar 的稻草人还使用特定物种的求救信号来驱散鸟类并记录活动，而 iCHASE 销售的系统可以通过计算机视觉检测鸟类，并用移动激光瞄准它们，根据需要调整其响应。
诺兹科娃说，她的护城河是系统的广度和 Flox 在现场收集的数据，她称之为“真正使驼鹿或灰熊安全移动的基本事实”。
“物理人工智能正在走出工厂，进入杂乱、生机勃勃的户外，”诺兹科娃说。 “每台在室外运行的机器——火车、卡车、无人机、拖拉机、机器人——都需要了解自然，而自然智能是感知堆栈的下一层。几乎没有人在建造它。”
迄今为止，该公司已在种子前和种子轮融资中筹集了约 500 万美元，种子轮融资由 Unconventional Ventures 和 Tilia Impact Ventures 领投。 Nozkova 表示，各轮融资的联合投资者包括 GENIUS NY、Norrsken、Satgana 和天使投资者。
该公司目前正在启动 1000 万美元的 A 轮融资，主要用于将大约 150 台设备增加到数千台部署单元，并将底层系统扩展到当前的野生动物用例之外。

Secret scanning works best when developers are confident in the findings. Catch too little, and real credentials can remain in a repository. Alert too often, and developers may spend time investigating strings that aren’t secrets.

Generic secrets make that balance especially difficult. The same string could be a real credential or a documentation placeholder, so detecting it requires understanding the surrounding code and text.

To address this challenge, we trained a secret classifier specifically for GitHub’s product needs: distinguishing real credentials from lookalikes while meeting the speed and efficiency requirements of scanning at scale.

In our companion post, Secret protection must scale with software, we explained why secret protection must keep pace with AI-accelerated development. Here, we go behind the scenes of the context-aware classifier powering that effort: how we designed, trained, and evaluated it to find more real secrets with less noise.
GitHub secret scanning operates at two key moments:

We developed a fast classifier that reduced median post-push scan execution time by 86% compared with the previous LLM-based pipeline. That efficiency made it practical to extend generic secret detection to push protection, returning results before developers push changes, not only after code is committed.

Structured credentials often include a distinctive prefix, length, alphabet, or checksum. Generic secrets may not. Their syntax overlaps with build identifiers, checksums, asset hashes, sample values, and other non-sensitive strings. Context is the deciding signal.

These cases are hard negatives: strings that match a credential pattern but are not usable credentials. Adding more rules can suppress some of them, but each exception risks hiding a real secret. A learned classifier can instead use signals such as file path, secret type, variable names, and nearby code or text.
That is why we shipped a new scanner using a two-stage pipeline:

As content is scanned, regex patterns cast a wide net and flag anything that looks like a credential, so real secrets aren’t missed at the start. Each candidate then goes to a fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier, which reads the value together with its file path, variable names, and surrounding code. The classifier estimates how likely it is to be a real secret. High-confidence findings become alerts, and lookalikes such as placeholders, test fixtures, and checksums are filtered out before they reach developers.
HOW OUR PIPELINE WORKS
Repository content, commits, pull requests, and other scanned surfaces.
Regex patterns identify possible tokens, keys, and credential-like strings.
Fine-tuned ModernBERT evaluates candidate + context and assigns likelihood of a true secret.
High-confidence findings move forward; likely false positives are filtered.

STEP 2 Generate candidates Regex patterns identify possible tokens, keys, and credential-like strings. STEP 3 Classify Fine-tuned ModernBERT evaluates candidate + context and assigns likelihood of a true secret. STEP 4 Alert or suppress High-confidence findings move forward; likely false positives are filtered. Connection: Scan to Generate candidates. Connection: Generate candidates to Classify. The important design choice is that the model does not replace deterministic scanning. Instead, it complements it. Regexes remain the right tool for finding candidate strings quickly. The classifier is used where machine learning provides the most leverage: distinguishing “looks like a secret” from “is likely a real secret.”

Most false positives are not random. They are hard negatives: strings that match a credential pattern but are not usable credentials. Examples include documentation placeholders, toy examples in tests, redacted values, non-sensitive IDs, and generated fixtures. These cases are easy for a regex to match and hard for a purely rule-based system to suppress without accidentally losing real secrets.

ModernBERT helps because it can read the candidate together with nearby code and text providing contextual understanding comparable to an LLM without the latency and computational overhead of generating natural-language output. For example, a candidate surrounded by words like “example,” “dummy,” “fake,” or “replace-me” may be lower risk than a candidate assigned to an environment variable in a deployment file. The classifier learns these contextual differences from labeled examples rather than requiring engineers to encode every exception as another rule.

We chose ModernBERT because it provides a strong fit for this workload: it is compact, efficient, and well suited for classification over code-adjacent text. For secret scanning, the model needs to make a calibrated decision over short candidate windows with high throughput and low latency.

That makes a fine-tuned encoder classifier a better serving shape than a general-purpose LLM for this stage of the pipeline. The model can be trained directly on our decision boundary, and evaluated using the same recall and precision metrics that matter to secret scanning quality.
The challenge was finding representative data for cases in which syntax alone is misleading. The training and evaluation strategy combines three sources:

Synthetic rows pass deterministic validation and model-based quality review before inclusion. Training emphasizes real secrets, realistic false positives, and hard negatives that frequently confuse regex-only approaches. Each model input includes the candidate value, file path, secret type, and a bounded amount of surrounding context. We select thresholds through offline evaluation and then validate behavior on production-like traffic before broader rollout.
Before splitting the data, we grouped rows that share a repository, candidate value, or example so near-duplicates could not appear in both training and evaluation.

Training focused on the cases that matter most for alert quality: real secrets, realistic false positives, and hard negatives that regexes frequently match. The input representation includes the candidate secret string, file path, type and a bounded amount of surrounding context. The output is a classification score used by the scanner to decide whether the candidate should proceed.

We optimized for the product tradeoff: preserve or improve recall while reducing false positives and serving cost. In practice, that means the classifier threshold is selected using offline evaluation, then validated against production-like traffic before rollout.

The most important training principle was to make the model see the confusing examples. We included candidates that are syntactically similar to real secrets but semantically different, so the model learns not only what a secret looks like, but also what a false positive looks like in context.
The trained model is exported to ONNX format with 8-bit quantization, enabling fast inference.
We evaluated the new pipeline’s impact in production in two stages: first against the production baseline on the same public traffic and then through a customer A/B experiment.

The best security tool is the one developers trust enough to use. Higher precision means fewer distracting alerts. Higher recall means more real secrets are caught. Lower cost means we can keep improving coverage without making scanning prohibitively expensive.

For developers and security teams, this should translate into fewer false positives, and faster feedback in the places where secrets are most likely to be introduced: commits, pull requests, and everyday development workflows.

Hybrid systems are powerful. Regex gives us speed, transparency, and broad candidate coverage. ModernBERT gives us learned context understanding and false-positive reduction. The combination outperforms either approach used alone for this product constraint.

We also learned that model size is not the same as model usefulness. A smaller fine-tuned classifier can be the right answer when the task is narrow, the decision boundary is measurable, and serving efficiency is critical.
This is one step toward making secret scanning more accurate, scalable, and easy to use. Looking ahead, we are focused on two areas:

As a Partner Applied Science Manager in Microsoft CoreAI, I lead an applied research team that measurably boosts developer productivity with ML and AI. We evolve GitHub Copilot in Completion, Chat, Code Review, and agentic workflows by continuously refining models and applying in-context learning for deeper, context-aware assistance.
Developers aren’t becoming more careless; they’re being outpaced. The tools that let developers create more software should also take on more of the work of protecting it.
We’re launching ReviewBench, a benchmark for code review agents built on representative GitHub pull requests, multi-source ground truth, calibrated evaluation, and production-aligned metrics.

所有者加权警报精度
推送后扫描
紧凑模型与远程 LLM 调用
JavaScript 绘制连接这些卡片的箭头。我们的管道对比之前的 LLM 管道 更智能的秘密扫描，成本仅为一小部分 接受度提高 11.5% 所有者加权警报精度 扫描执行时间中位数降低 86% 推送后扫描 服务成本降低 98% 紧凑模型与远程 LLM 调用相比
当开发人员对结果充满信心时，秘密扫描效果最佳。捕获的信息太少，真实的凭据可能会保留在存储库中。警报太频繁，开发人员可能会花时间调查不属于秘密的字符串。
通用秘密使这种平衡变得特别困难。相同的字符串可能是真实的凭据或文档占位符，因此检测它需要了解周围的代码和文本。
为了应对这一挑战，我们专门针对 GitHub 的产品需求训练了一个秘密分类器：区分真实凭证和相似凭证，同时满足大规模扫描的速度和效率要求。
在我们的姊妹篇《秘密保护必须随软件扩展》中，我们解释了为什么秘密保护必须跟上人工智能加速发展的步伐。在这里，我们深入了解上下文感知分类器的幕后故事：我们如何设计、训练和评估它，以更少的噪音找到更多真实的秘密。
GitHub 秘密扫描在两个关键时刻进行：
我们开发了一种快速分类器，与之前基于 LLM 的管道相比，该分类器将中值推后扫描执行时间缩短了 86%。这种效率使得将通用秘密检测扩展到推送保护变得可行，在开发人员推送更改之前返回结果，而不仅仅是在提交代码之后。
结构化凭证通常包括独特的前缀、长度、字母表或校验和。一般秘密可能不会。它们的语法与构建标识符、校验和、资产哈希、样本值和其他非敏感字符串重叠。上下文是决定信号。
这些情况是硬性否定：与凭证模式匹配的字符串，但不是可用的凭证。添加更多规则可以抑制其中一些规则，但每个例外都有隐藏真正秘密的风险。学习的分类器可以使用文件路径、秘密类型、变量名称以及附近的代码或文本等信号。
这就是我们使用两级管道交付新扫描仪的原因：
当内容被扫描时，正则表达式模式会撒下一张大网并标记任何看起来像凭证的东西，因此从一开始就不会错过真正的秘密。然后，每个候选者都会进入一个经过微调的 ModernBERT 分类器，该分类器会读取该值及其文件路径、变量名称和周围的代码。分类器估计它是真正秘密的可能性。高可信度的发现会成为警报，而占位符、测试装置和校验和等类似内容在到达开发人员之前会被过滤掉。
我们的管道如何运作
存储库内容、提交、拉取请求和其他扫描表面。
正则表达式模式识别可能的标记、密钥和类似凭证的字符串。
经过微调的 ModernBERT 评估候选者 + 上下文并分配真实秘密的可能性。
高可信度的研究结果向前推进；可能的误报被过滤掉。

JavaScript 绘制连接这些卡片的箭头。我们的管道如何工作 首先广泛，第二仔细 第 1 步 扫描存储库内容、提交、拉取请求和其他扫描表面。步骤 2 生成候选正则表达式模式识别可能的令牌、密钥和类似凭证的字符串。步骤 3 分类微调 ModernBERT 评估候选者 + 上下文并分配真实秘密的可能性。第 4 步 警告或抑制高可信度的发现向前推进；可能的误报被过滤掉。连接：扫描生成候选人。连接：生成候选者进行分类。连接：分类为警报或抑制。
重要的设计选择是该模型不会取代确定性扫描。相反，它是对它的补充。正则表达式仍然是快速查找候选字符串的正确工具。分类器用于机器学习提供最大影响力的地方：区分“看起来像秘密”和“可能是真正的秘密”。
大多数误报不是随机的。它们是硬否定：与凭证模式匹配但不是可用凭证的字符串。示例包括文档占位符、测试中的玩具示例、编辑值、非敏感 ID 和生成的装置。这些情况对于正则表达式来说很容易匹配，而对于纯粹基于规则的系统来说很难在不意外丢失真正秘密的情况下抑制。
ModernBERT 很有帮助，因为它可以读取候选人以及附近的代码和文本，提供与法学硕士相当的上下文理解，而无需生成自然语言输出的延迟和计算开销。例如，被“example”、“dummy”、“fake”或“replace-me”等词语包围的候选者可能比分配给部署文件中的环境变量的候选者风险更低。分类器从标记的示例中学习这些上下文差异，而不是要求工程师将每个异常编码为另一个规则。
我们选择 ModernBERT 是因为它非常适合这种工作负载：它紧凑、高效，并且非常适合对代码相邻文本进行分类。对于秘密扫描，模型需要在高吞吐量和低延迟的短候选窗口上做出校准决策。
这使得经过微调的编码器分类器在管道的这一阶段比通用 LLM 具有更好的服务形状。该模型可以直接在我们的决策边界上进行训练，并使用对秘密扫描质量至关重要的相同召回率和精度指标进行评估。
挑战在于找到仅语法具有误导性的案例的代表性数据。培训和评估策略结合了三个来源：
合成行在纳入之前要通过确定性验证和基于模型的质量审查。培训强调真正的秘密、现实的误报和硬否定，这些经常会混淆纯正则表达式的方法。每个模型输入包括候选值、文件路径、秘密类型和有限数量的周围上下文。我们通过离线评估选择阈值，然后在更广泛的推广之前验证类似生产流量的行为。
在分割数据之前，我们对共享存储库、候选值或示例的行进行分组，以便在训练和评估中不会出现接近重复的数据。
培训重点关注对警报质量最重要的案例：真正的秘密、现实的误报以及正则表达式经常匹配的硬阴性。输入表示包括候选秘密字符串、文件路径、类型和有限数量的周围上下文。输出是扫描仪用来决定候选人是否应该继续进行的分类分数。
我们针对产品​​权衡进行了优化：保留或提高召回率，同时减少误报和服务成本。实际上，这意味着使用离线评估来选择分类器阈值，然后在推出之前针对类似生产的流量进行验证。
最重要的训练原则是让模型看到令人困惑的例子。我们纳入了在语法上与真实秘密相似但在语义上不同的候选者，因此模型不仅可以学习秘密的外观，还可以了解误报在上下文中的外观。
训练后的模型将导出为具有 8 位量化的 ONNX 格式，从而实现快速推理。
我们分两个阶段评估了新管道对生产的影响：首先根据相同公共流量的生产基线，然后通过客户 A/B 实验。
最好的安全工具是开发人员足够信任并使用的工具。更高的精度意味着更少的干扰警报。更高的召回率意味着更多真正的秘密被捕获。较低的成本意味着我们可以不断提高覆盖范围，而无需使扫描成本过高。
对于开发人员和安全团队来说，这应该意味着更少的误报，以及在最有可能引入秘密的地方（提交、拉取请求和日常开发工作流程）更快的反馈。
混合系统功能强大。正则表达式为我们提供了速度、透明度和广泛的候选人覆盖范围。 ModernBERT 为我们提供了学习上下文理解和误报减少。对于该产品限制，该组合的性能优于单独使用的任何一种方法。
我们还了解到，模型大小与模型有用性不同。当任务很窄、决策边界可测量并且服务效率至关重要时，较小的微调分类器可能是正确的答案。
这是使秘密扫描更加准确、可扩展且易于使用的一步。展望未来，我们将重点关注两个领域：
非常感谢 GitHub 和 Microsoft 的工程、科学和产品团队帮助构建了这个新的秘密扫描器的训练数据、评估套件、服务堆栈和推出计划。
作为 Microsoft CoreAI 的高级研究科学家，我为 GitHub Copilot 开发代理模型编排和路由技术。我的研究重点是自适应模型选择、多模型协调、长期代理工作流程和开发人员安全。
作为 Microsoft CoreAI 的合作伙伴应用科学经理，我领导一个应用研究团队，通过 ML 和 AI 显着提高开发人员的工作效率。我们通过不断完善模型并应用上下文学习来获得更深入的上下文感知帮助，从而在完成、聊天、代码审查和代理工作流程方面改进 GitHub Copilot。
开发人员并没有变得更加粗心，而是变得更加粗心。他们正在被超越。让开发人员创建更多软件的工具也应该承担更多的保护软件的工作。
我们正在推出 ReviewBench，这是一个基于代表性 GitHub 拉取请求、多源地面事实、校准评估和生产对齐指标构建的代码审查代理基准。

fulltext: LFM2.5-24B-A2B builds on LFM2-24B-A2B and keeps its architecture: 40 layers, 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing, and the same hybrid of gated short convolutions and GQA. The context window grows from 32K to 131K tokens, and an in-place tokenizer expansion doubles the vocabulary from 65K to 128K tokens for better non-Latin tokenization. Unlike its predecessor, it is a reasoning-only model that produces an explicit chain of thought before its final answer.

Pre-training was scaled up from ~17T to ~33T tokens. Mid-training then adds 2T tokens at 32K context, weighted toward reasoning, math, code, instruction following, and multilingual text, and 300B tokens at 131K context, weighted toward long-context data. Tool calls and multi-turn trajectories appear throughout both phases. Post-training turns the base model into an agent in five stages:

We evaluated LFM2.5-24B-A2B against Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning on 16 benchmarks covering tool use and agentic workflows, knowledge, instruction following, math, and coding. It is the smallest model in the group, yet it is competitive with MoEs with ~50% more total and active parameters.
*All the models were evaluated with vLLM, using each benchmark's recommended generation parameters.

For your app, the strengths are tool use and instruction following. LFM2.5-24B-A2B leads or matches the competition on five of the eight tool-use and agentic benchmarks (AutomationBench, BFCLv4, ToolSandbox, LiveClaw, and τ³-Bench Banking), and on AutomationBench it scores more than three times the next-best model. It also leads on all three instruction-following benchmarks. Larger models keep an edge on knowledge-heavy benchmarks like GPQA Diamond, HLE, and AA-Omniscience, and on coding benchmarks like SWE-Bench Verified (OpenCode) and SciCode, so pair LFM2.5-24B-A2B with retrieval or web search for knowledge-heavy workloads.
These results make LFM2.5-24B-A2B a strong foundation for agents that need to reason, call tools, and run reliably on your device.
LFM2.5-24B-A2B ships with day-one support across the inference ecosystem, including llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, and ONNX.

Edge inference. LFM2.5-24B-A2B is the fastest of the compared MoEs, decoding 184 tokens/s on an M5 Max and 114 tokens/s on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395. That is up to 1.7x faster than the next-best model, while using the least memory.
GPU inference. LFM2.5-24B-A2B is the fastest model in its size class, reaching over 21K output tokens per second at high concurrency on a single B300.
Reach for LFM2.5-24B-A2B when you need agents that reason, call tools, and run reliably on your device.

对于您的应用程序，优势在于工具使用和遵循说明。 LFM2.5-24B-A2B 在八个工具使用和代理基准测试中的五个（AutomationBench、BFCLv4、ToolSandbox、LiveClaw 和 τ³-Bench Banking）上领先或匹配竞争对手，并且在 AutomationBench 上的得分是次优模型的三倍多。它还在所有三个指令遵循基准测试中处于领先地位。较大的模型在 GPQA Diamond、HLE 和 AA-Omniscience 等知识密集型基准测试以及 SWE-Bench Verified (OpenCode) 和 SciCode 等编码基准测试上保持优势，因此将 LFM2.5-24B-A2B 与知识密集型工作负载的检索或 Web 搜索配对。
